newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PNG stocks jump after PM Chan stands aside.
newsitem.headline: PNG stocks jump after PM Chan stands aside.

text.p: Papua New Guinea-linked stocks listed in Australia jumped in active early trade on Thursday after Prime Minister Sir Julius Chan stood aside to end 10 days of political turmoil over his hiring of mercenaries.
"Everyone is relieved that the parliamentary process actually worked and that we didn't go into a period of military control," ABN AMRO Hoare Govett Head of Mining Research David Walker said.
Orogen Minerals Ltd, which is 51-percent owned by the PNG government, rose 13 cents to A$3.15 (US$2.48) in early trading, while Oil Search Ltd rose 11 cents to A$2.68 on heavy volume.
Lihir Gold Ltd rose six cents to A$2.19 while Niugini Mining Ltd was unchanged at A$2.95.

Bougainville Copper Ltd, which controls the vast disused Panguna copper mine on Bougainville island, rose five cents to 60 cents despite the failure of Chan's plan to use mercenaries to crush the Bougainville uprising and retake the mine.

Chan told parliament on Wednesday that he was stepping aside to make way for a caretaker administration while an inquiry was held into the US$36 million contract with British mercenary firm Sandline International.

"It's positive that Chan's resigned and it should calm the situation up there somewhat," said ANZ Securities gold analyst David Kauler. "It is a cheap time to be buying some of those PNG stocks, particularly Lihir on the gold side," Kauler said.
But investors were expected to remain tentative in the next six months while a new government was elected and its resources policy was formed. Elections are due in June.
"There's been no suggestion that resources policy should change," Kauler said.

"This latest saga really hasn't had a lot to do with foreign companies operating their resources projects in PNG, it's had more to do with the issue of hiring mercenaries to kill PNG nationals," he added.
